title: G-Code Optimization for CNC Milling Operations

content.objective: To program, simulate, and machine an aluminum 6061 slot-and-pocket profile using optimized G-code and carbide end-mills.
content.theory: Subtractive CNC milling relies on precise feeds (F) and spindle speeds (S) derived from cutting velocity formulas: Vc = (π * D * N) / 1000 to maximize tool life and achieve surface finish Ra < 1.6 µm.
procedure: Clamp stock securely in the precision milling vice and perform edge-finding to set G54 work coordinate zero.
Program roughing pockets using circular interpolation (G02/G03) with 1.5mm step-down passes.
Apply finish contouring pass using cutter radius compensation (G41).
Execute the machining program with flood coolant and measure final dimensions.
content.conclusion: Dimensional accuracy on pocket depth was within ±0.025mm of design specifications with zero chatter marks.
